data.content_ref: inline:The Pragmatic Wager (a0b919ae506615d2) depends on the rejection of inductive probability as a necessary condition for rational action. This relation is refuted if it can be demonstrated that preferring the better-corroborated theory logically entails an assumption that the future will resemble the past, thereby making the 'pragmatic wager' indistinguishable from the inductive principle Popper explicitly rejects.
